title: Embedding a reduced finite-type algebra into finitely many extension fields
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] [def-pc-field-extension] and $B$ a reduced commutative $k$-algebra, meaning that $b^n=0$ with $n\ge1$ implies $b=0$. Assume $B$ is generated as a $k$-algebra by finitely many elements. Then there exist an integer $t\ge0$, extension fields $K_i/k$ for $1\le i\le t$, and an injective unital $k$-algebra homomorphism $j:B\hookrightarrow\prod_{i=1}^tK_i$. The product has coordinatewise ring operations and scalar action; for $t=0$ it is the zero ring. The zero algebra $B$ is allowed, in which case one may take $t=0$. No perfectness of $k$ or integrality of $B$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 034N (lemma-geometrically-reduced-any-reduced-base-change), proof, second sentence: the finite-type reduced algebra embedding into a finite product of fields.

proof.text: If $B$ is the zero ring, take $t=0$ and the unique map from $B$ to the empty product. Both rings have one element, so this is an injective unital $k$-algebra map. Henceforth assume $B\ne0$.

source.place: Tag 034N (lemma-geometrically-reduced-any-reduced-base-change), finite-product reduction; empty-product convention of the item

proof.text: Apply [lem-wf-affine-noetherian-components] to the finitely generated $k$-algebra $B$: it is Noetherian. By [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finitely-many-minimal-primes], its minimal prime ideals form a finite set; enumerate them without repetition as $\mathfrak p_1,\ldots,\mathfrak p_t$.

For each $i$ put $K_i=B_{\mathfrak p_i}$ with its canonical map $\lambda_i:B\to K_i$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Since $B$ is reduced and $\mathfrak p_i$ is minimal, [lem-weil-pbc-minimal-prime-reduced-localization-field] says $K_i$ is a field. Give $K_i$ the scalar map $k\to B\xrightarrow{\lambda_i}K_i$; this makes it an extension field of $k$ by [def-pc-field-extension].

Define $j(b)=(\lambda_i(b))_{i=1}^t$. The maps $\lambda_i$ are unital ring maps, so the coordinatewise operations make $j$ a unital ring map. For $a\in k$ and $b\in B$, its $i$th coordinate satisfies $\lambda_i(ab)=\lambda_i(a)\lambda_i(b)$, exactly the scalar action just assigned to $K_i$. Thus $j$ is a $k$-algebra homomorphism.

If $j(b)=0$, then $b/1=0$ in every $B_{\mathfrak p_i}$. The fraction equality in [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] gives $s_i\notin\mathfrak p_i$ with $s_i b=0$. Primality implies $b\in\mathfrak p_i$, since $s_i b\in\mathfrak p_i$ and $s_i\notin\mathfrak p_i$. Hence $b$ belongs to every minimal prime of $B$.

Every prime $\mathfrak q$ of $B$ contains a minimal prime by [lem-weil-pbc-prime-contains-minimal-prime], applied with $I=0$. Therefore the element $b$ of Step 5 lies in every prime. By [lem-weil-pbc-zero-locus-eq-iff-radical-eq], with $I=0$, it belongs to $\sqrt{(0)}$: $b^n=0$ for some $n\ge1$. Reducedness gives $b=0$. If $j(b)=j(c)$, apply this to $b-c$ to obtain $b=c$. This proves injectivity and all the required assertions.
